findings.finding: answerCallbackQuery's single WARN log scrubs the exception message via TelegramApiClient.scrubTokens before logging. Endpoint path is a constant template (/bot{token}/answerCallbackQuery) bound by RestClient; our code never logs the raw URL. No plaintext token can reach the log.

Ack path decrypts the token per-call inside sendOnce (unchanged AES-GCM path); decrypted token is a local, never stored as a field, serialized, or logged. Plaintext-token lifetime invariant preserved.

Endpoint paths are constant literals; callbackQueryId/text/replyMarkup are placed in the JSON request body (Jackson-encoded), never in the request URL. reply_markup url-button values are opaque body content forwarded to Telegram and never dereferenced by the backend. Strict http(s) URL-scheme validation for buttons is Task 4 (validateSteps on activate), out of scope for this sender task.

Test token literal (1234567890:ABCdefGHI_...) is a synthetic well-formed shape, not a real Telegram token, encrypted with the test-profile placeholder key (0*64 from application-test.properties). No real credentials introduced.
Best-effort swallow with WARN-only and no audit event matches Decision 8 (non-content ack must not block funnel advance). Acceptable; not a security-relevant monitoring gap.
